feed.title: 一孔录 · Reading the classics word by word
feed.subtitle: Every line Yikonglu has read aloud can be checked here.

entry.title: 5.11 What I do not wish others to do to me
entry.summary: 子贡曰：我不欲人之加诸我也，吾亦欲无加诸人。子曰：赐也，非尔所及也。 —— The difference is one character, wu “there is none” against wu “do not”: having no such impulse at all is humaneness; having it and restraining it is reciprocity. What Zigong described is the humane person's naturalness, which he has not reached. Today: someone who hates being woken by messages at night schedules every message after 10 pm to send the next morning.

entry.title: 5.10 I have never seen anyone who is truly firm
entry.summary: 子曰：吾未见刚者。或对曰：申枨。子曰：枨也欲，焉得刚？ —— Firmness holds things down; desire is being covered by things. Looking hard and loving to win may mean being led by one's own desires. Today: the person who speaks most aggressively in meetings and yields to no one cannot walk past a mall sale.

entry.title: 5.9 Zai Yu slept in the daytime
entry.summary: 宰予昼寝。子曰：朽木不可雕也，粪土之墙不可杇也，于予与何诛？子曰：始吾于人也，听其言而信其行；今吾于人也，听其言而观其行。于予与改是。 —— The point is not the nap but a slackened will and words that deeds do not match. “Not worth rebuking” is the heaviest rebuke. Confucius used the occasion to set a rule: hear the words, and also watch the conduct. Today: three gym memberships in a year, and not one visit.

entry.title: 5.8 Who is better, you or Hui?
entry.summary: 子谓子贡曰：女与回也孰愈？对曰：赐也何敢望回？回也闻一以知十，赐也闻一以知二。子曰：弗如也！吾与女弗如也。 —— Confucius's question tests whether Zigong sees himself clearly. He does, and does not find it hard to bow, so Confucius first says “you are not his equal” and then solemnly affirms him. Today: a coach asks two players who is stronger, and one points at the other without a second thought.

entry.title: 5.7 Meng Wubo asked whether Zilu was humane
entry.summary: 孟武伯问：子路仁乎？子曰：不知也。又问。子曰：由也，千乘之国，可使治其赋也，不知其仁也。求也何如？子曰：求也，千室之邑，百乘之家，可使为之宰也，不知其仁也。赤也何如？子曰：赤也，束带立于朝，可使与宾客言也，不知其仁也。 —— Say plainly what visible ability there is; humaneness comes and goes, and one does not vouch for it. Three students, three talents: each line says what they can do, none says they are humane. Today: in a background check, the referee says “I vouch for his skills; his character I can't speak to”.

entry.title: 5.6 If the Way does not prevail, I will take a raft out to sea
entry.summary: 子曰：道不行，乘桴浮于海。从我者，其由与？子路闻之喜。子曰：由也好勇过我，无所取材。 —— Going out to sea is a sigh, a figure of speech; Zilu took it literally, with courage to spare but no sense of measuring what is fitting. Today: someone in the group chat says offhand they'll quit and travel the world, and someone else packs a bag that very night.

entry.title: 5.5 The Master wished Qidiao Kai to take office
entry.summary: 子使漆雕开仕。对曰：吾斯之未能信。子说。 —— Whether one's ability is enough, a teacher can see; the hair-thin part not truly gained inside, only oneself knows. Admitting that hair is refusing to rest in small achievement, so Confucius was glad. Today: offered a promotion, she says she can't carry that role yet and asks for another six months.

entry.title: 5.4 Yong is humane but not glib
entry.summary: 或曰：雍也仁而不佞。子曰：焉用佞？御人以口给，屡憎于人。不知其仁，焉用佞？ —— The root problem is “no real substance”: a quick, argumentative tongue with nothing true in it wins more dislike the more it talks. Confucius did not grant Zhonggong humaneness because humaneness is too great to grant lightly. Today: the person who takes on everything, agrees to everything and delivers nothing finds colleagues walking around him three months later.

entry.title: 5.3 Zigong asked: What about me?
entry.summary: 子贡问曰：赐也何如？子曰：女，器也。曰：何器也？曰：瑚琏也。 —— Two layers in one line: not yet “not a vessel”, but the most precious kind of vessel; praise with direction in it. Today: the boss says “you're the most useful person on my team”, and it feels good at the time but not quite right on the way home.

entry.title: 5.2 Of Zijian the Master said: A gentleman indeed is this man
entry.summary: 子谓子贱：君子哉若人！鲁无君子者，斯焉取斯？ —— A person's virtue is taken from the worthies around him, so praising him means also praising those who made him. Today: a newcomer wins an award and the first thing said on stage is to point to a teacher in the audience.

entry.title: 5.1 Gongye Chang is fit to be given a wife
entry.summary: 子谓公冶长：可妻也。虽在缧绁之中，非其罪也。以其子妻之。子谓南容：邦有道不废，邦无道免于刑戮。以其兄之子妻之。 —— What matters is not that Confucius was tolerant, but the one judgement “was the crime his or not”: a prison imposed from outside is not his honour or shame. The Nan Rong section says that care in word and deed stands firm in good times and bad. Today: someone once wrongly disciplined and later cleared — some people avoid him, others keep handing him the important work.

entry.title: 4.26 Importune a ruler and you meet disgrace; importune a friend and you grow distant
entry.summary: 子游曰：事君数，斯辱矣；朋友数，斯疏矣。 —— Persuasion has limits. When it does not get through, stop (with a ruler, leave); urging too often only pushes people away.

entry.title: 4.25 Virtue is not solitary; it is sure to have neighbours
entry.summary: 子曰：德不孤，必有邻。 —— This is not “good deeds are rewarded”; it is like answering like. What you hold to draws people who hold to the same thing.

entry.title: 4.24 The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and quick in action
entry.summary: 子曰：君子欲讷于言而敏于行。 —— Of the easy end and the hard end, rein in the easy one (speaking) and spur on the hard one (doing). It is not refusing to speak, but not talking loosely.

entry.title: 4.23 Those who err through restraint are few
entry.summary: 子曰：以约失之者鲜矣。 —— Holding back words, temper and display are all restraint, not only money. Today: the person who moves house with only two boxes is the one who loses nothing.

entry.title: 4.22 The ancients did not let words out, ashamed that their conduct would not keep up
entry.summary: 子曰：古者言之不出，耻躬之不逮也。 —— The fear is not of saying something wrong but of failing to do it. Today: in the work group chat one person replies “I'll definitely hand it in this week”; another says nothing and hands it in on Wednesday.

entry.title: 4.21 One must know the ages of one's parents
entry.summary: 子曰：父母之年，不可不知也。一则以喜，一则以惧。 —— Joy and fear are the same fact: one more day lived is one day fewer left. Today: the phone calendar reminds you of a parent's birthday once a year, and the number grows every year.

entry.title: 4.20 For three years not altering his father's way
entry.summary: 子曰：三年无改于父之道，可谓孝矣。 —— The half sentence must be read with the half before it; “do not alter for three years” cannot be taken alone as an iron rule. Today: when young we remember only half of what our parents said, and recall the other half only after running a household ourselves.

entry.title: 4.19 While parents live, do not travel far; if you travel, have a fixed direction
entry.summary: 子曰：父母在，不远游，游必有方。 —— If you can avoid travelling far, do; if you must go, let your parents know where you are. Today: landing on a business trip, first drop a location pin in the family group.

entry.title: 4.18 In serving parents, remonstrate gently
entry.summary: 子曰：事父母几谏，见志不从，又敬不违，劳而不怨。 —— Not silence, but a low voice; if it does not get through, do not turn hostile, but try again another time. The Neize line “挞之流血不敢疾怨” (even if beaten till one bleeds, dare not resent) is an ancient ritual demand, and the video says plainly that it is not to be copied today. Today: a parent forwards a fake advert to the family group; one child replies “fake again”, another phones privately and explains slowly.

entry.title: 4.17 Seeing a worthy, think of equalling him; seeing an unworthy, look inward
entry.summary: 子曰：见贤思齐焉，见不贤而内自省也。 —— The people one sees are good and bad; each time, fold it back onto oneself. Today: scrolling past a peer's fine work, one person sneers “just luck”, another quietly saves the tutorial.

entry.title: 4.16 The gentleman understands rightness; the small man understands profit
entry.summary: 子曰：君子喻于义，小人喻于利。 —— Both sides use the same kind of “understanding”; the difference is which thing they have understood through and through. Today: someone selling a second-hand item finds a scratch not in the listing, and changes “90% new” to “70% new” on their own.

entry.title: 4.15 My Way is threaded through by one
entry.summary: 子曰：参乎！吾道一以贯之。曾子曰：唯。子出，门人问曰：何谓也？曾子曰：夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。 —— “Loyalty and reciprocity” do not say the Way in full; they hand the learner something to hold. “Threaded through by one” is said only to the one who is ready to understand it. Today: an old craftsman tells the apprentice just one thing: do your own step through to the end, then think of the person who takes over next.

entry.title: 4.14 Worry not about having no post, but about what you stand on
entry.summary: 子曰：不患无位，患所以立。不患莫己知，求为可知也。 —— It is not about finding ways to be noticed; it is about first having the substance worth noticing. Whether a post is given, whether others know you, is not in your hands. Today: dozens of résumés with no reply; one person blames the blind employers, another redoes every project in his portfolio.

entry.title: 4.13 Can one govern a state with ritual and yielding?
entry.summary: 子曰：能以礼让为国乎？何有？不能以礼让为国，如礼何？ —— Yielding is the lining inside ritual. When only the outward form is left, ritual itself no longer works, never mind governing a state. Today: a wedding banquet with every seat and formality in order, and the two families quarrel over who sits at the head table until the guests leave.

entry.title: 4.12 Act by what profits you, and resentment multiplies
entry.summary: 子曰：放于利而行，多怨。 —— The resentment does not come from the word “profit”; it comes from profiting only oneself. Today: the flatmate who never buys the shared things and uses them most finds no one seeing him off the day he moves out.

entry.title: 4.11 The gentleman cherishes virtue, the petty man his comfort
entry.summary: 子曰：君子怀德，小人怀土；君子怀刑，小人怀惠。 —— “Cherishing one's ground” is not homesickness; it is a heart that guards only its own little comfort. The whole difference between gentleman and petty man lies between public and private. Today: two people receive the same job offer in another city; one asks first what he can learn and whom he can help, the other only which place is more comfortable to stay in.

entry.title: 4.10 No fixed yes, no fixed no; side with what is right
entry.summary: 子曰：君子之于天下也，无适也，无莫也，义之与比。 —— Do not decide in advance and do not refuse in advance; look only at whether it accords with what is right. “Nothing allowed, nothing forbidden” without rightness in charge is mere recklessness. Today: a line judge does not decide beforehand who should win, but bends down to see whether this one ball touched the line.

entry.title: 4.9 A scholar set on the Way who is ashamed of poor clothes
entry.summary: 子曰：士志于道，而耻恶衣恶食者，未足与议也。 —— The mouth says the heart is set on the Way, but the heart is ordered about by things outside. The problem is not dressing poorly; it is treating poor dress as a shame. Today: someone who says he will devote himself to studying for the exam first spends three days picking the most expensive stationery.

entry.title: 4.8 Hear the Way in the morning, die content at dusk
entry.summary: 子曰：朝闻道，夕死可矣。 —— The hard part is not hearing, but still believing after one has heard. Life and death are the great matter; without something truly gained in the heart, no one can say “I may die at dusk.” Today: an old man in a hospital bed finally sees through what he never understood in a lifetime, takes his daughter's hand and says, “Now I am at peace.”

entry.title: 4.7 People's faults each follow their kind
entry.summary: 子曰：人之过也，各于其党。观过，斯知仁矣。 —— Whether a fault leans too generous or too mean shows whether one is humane. Today: two people are half an hour late — one took a fallen old man to hospital, one overslept.

entry.title: 4.6 I have not seen one who loves humaneness
entry.summary: 子曰：我未见好仁者、恶不仁者。好仁者，无以尚之；恶不仁者，其为仁矣，不使不仁者加乎其身。有能一日用其力于仁矣乎？我未见力不足者。盖有之矣，我未之见也。 —— Where the heart goes, the strength goes; the hard part is not strength but willingness. Today: the person with no time to exercise scrolls the phone for two hours before bed.

entry.title: 4.5 Wealth and rank are what people want
entry.summary: 子曰：富与贵，是人之所欲也；不以其道得之，不处也。贫与贱，是人之所恶也；不以其道得之，不去也。君子去仁，恶乎成名？君子无终食之间违仁，造次必于是，颠沛必于是。 —— Do not take wealth that should not come, and do not dodge an undeserved poverty by crooked means; the big choices and the small daily work make each other. Today: the bus brakes hard, and the young man's first grab is to steady the old woman beside him.

entry.title: 4.4 Set your heart on humaneness and there is no evil
entry.summary: 子曰：苟志于仁矣，无恶也。 —— Resolve does not guarantee no mistakes; it guarantees no intention to do wrong. Today: a learner driver scrapes the car three times in a year but never once runs a red light.

entry.title: 4.3 Only the humane can love and hate others
entry.summary: 子曰：唯仁者能好人，能恶人。 —— Everyone can like and dislike; the “can” lies in doing it rightly, which requires a heart that is not tied to anything. Today: a competition judge who sees a former student take the stage stands up, leaves the panel and gives no score for that round.

entry.title: 4.2 The inhumane cannot long endure hardship
entry.summary: 子曰：不仁者不可以久处约，不可以长处乐。仁者安仁，知者利仁。 —— Long hardship makes people overstep, long pleasure makes them indulge; whether outside things can take a person away depends on whether the original heart is there. Today: someone out of work for six months still gets up at seven, shaves, and goes out for a run.

entry.title: 4.1 Living among the humane is beautiful
entry.summary: 子曰：里仁为美。择不处仁，焉得知？ —— Choose the wrong place to live and what you lose is not the house but the heart that tells right from wrong. Today: when buying a flat people ask about schools, the metro and sunlight, and rarely about how the neighbours treat one another.

entry.title: 3.26 High position without generosity
entry.summary: 子曰：居上不宽，为礼不敬，临丧不哀，吾何以观之哉？ —— It is not that it looks bad; there is nothing left to look at. Today: the man on the phone talking business at the door of the funeral hall — however large his gift, no one remembers he came.

entry.title: 3.25 The Shao is perfectly beautiful and perfectly good
entry.summary: 子谓韶：尽美矣，又尽善也。谓武：尽美矣，未尽善也。 —— The difference is in how it came: one was yielded, one was taken by force. Today: two equally splendid wins, one earned head-on, one after the opponent withdrew injured — the podium does not taste the same.

entry.title: 3.24 The border warden of Yi asks to see him
entry.summary: 仪封人请见，曰：君子之至于斯也，吾未尝不得见也。从者见之。出曰：二三子何患于丧乎？天下之无道也久矣，天将以夫子为木铎。 —— A minor official saw Confucius's weight at first sight. Today: an old teacher moved off the podium runs free classes in the community, and more people come than were ever in his class.

entry.title: 3.23 The Master speaks of music to the Grand Music Master of Lu
entry.summary: 子语鲁大师乐，曰：乐其可知也：始作，翕如也；从之，纯如也，皦如也，绎如也，以成。 —— First together, then harmonious, each part clear within the harmony, linked to the end. Today: a choir starts together, then blends, each voice part still audible, singing through in one breath.

entry.title: 3.22 Guan Zhong's capacity was small
entry.summary: 子曰：管仲之器小哉！或曰：管仲俭乎？曰：管氏有三归，官事不摄，焉得俭？然则管仲知礼乎？曰：邦君树塞门，管氏亦树塞门；邦君为两君之好，有反坫，管氏亦有反坫。管氏而知礼，孰不知礼？ —— Confucius does not say outright where the smallness lies; it shows in the luxury and usurpation. Today: the company grows, the boss's office becomes a palace, and the rules apply only to others.

entry.title: 3.21 Duke Ai asks about the altar of the soil
entry.summary: 哀公问社于宰我。宰我对曰：夏后氏以松，殷人以柏，周人以栗，曰：使民战栗。子闻之，曰：成事不说，遂事不谏，既往不咎。 —— The three “nots” are not “never mind” but a heavy rebuke, to make him careful in future. Today: forwarding an unverified message in a group chat — the recall button only works for two minutes.

entry.title: 3.20 The Guanju: joy without excess
entry.summary: 子曰：关雎乐而不淫，哀而不伤。 —— Not too little feeling, but feeling full without going over. Today: crying while reading your wedding vows, wiping your eyes and finishing the last line.

entry.title: 3.19 The lord employs his ministers with ritual
entry.summary: 定公问：君使臣，臣事君，如之何？孔子对曰：君使臣以礼，臣事君以忠。 —— Each side looks only at its own end; Duke Ding was the ruler, and his question was answered with his own half. Today: a team lead first asks whether people are treated with enough respect; the team member first asks whether the work is done properly.

entry.title: 3.18 Serving one's lord with full ritual
entry.summary: 子曰：事君尽礼，人以为谄也。 —— Not a bit extra — ritual simply requires this; Confucius says only “people take it for flattery”, with no insult back. Today: getting to the meeting early and filling in expense forms fully, and being mocked as a try-hard.

entry.title: 3.17 The sheep for announcing the new moon
entry.summary: 子贡欲去告朔之饩羊。子曰：赐也，尔爱其羊，我爱其礼。 —— The sheep marks the rite; keep the marker and the rite can still be recognised and restored. Today: an old shop that makes one pot of the old recipe at the winter solstice, not for sale.

entry.title: 3.16 In archery, piercing the hide is not the point
entry.summary: 子曰：射不主皮，为力不同科，古之道也。 —— The contest is in what can be trained, not in what you were born with.

entry.title: 3.15 In the Grand Temple he asked about everything
entry.summary: 子入大庙，每事问。或曰：孰谓鄹人之子知礼乎？入大庙，每事问。子闻之，曰：是礼也。 —— Thirty years in, you still double-check.

entry.title: 3.14 Zhou looked to the two dynasties
entry.summary: 子曰：周监于二代，郁郁乎文哉！吾从周。 —— Following Zhou means following the work of improving on predecessors bit by bit. Today: the dishes at New Year's Eve dinner.
